stem: Seven-year-old Lotta has vomited several times over the past 24 hours, with anorexia, low-grade fever, right lower quadrant abdominal pain that began periumbilically, WCC 18 with neutrophilia, an appendix measuring 8 mm on ultrasound, moderate free abdominal fluid, persistent fever and lethargy, and now generalised guarding. Which is the most appropriate next step?

options.text: Intravenous antibiotics, admit to the surgical ward and reassess every few hours.
Intravenous antibiotics, fluid resuscitation and urgent laparoscopy
Blood culture, repeat abdominal ultrasound after a few hours and withhold antibiotics until culture results have come back
Intravenous antibiotics and plan for semi-urgent appendectomy after a few weeks
Oral antibiotics, send child home and review clinically the next day

explanation: This presentation is consistent with complicated appendicitis with peritonitis (generalised guarding, free fluid, systemic features). The appropriate management is urgent surgical assessment with resuscitation, IV antibiotics, and urgent operative intervention rather than watchful waiting or delayed appendectomy.

citations.title: Practice Quiz: Emergency Medicine - Abdominal pain

rationale: Complicated appendicitis with peritoneal signs requires urgent operative management after initial resuscitation.

optionExplanations.A: Too conservative for perforated/complicated appendicitis with peritonitis.
optionExplanations.B: Correct: urgent laparoscopy after resuscitation and IV antibiotics is appropriate for suspected complicated appendicitis.
optionExplanations.C: Unsafe to delay treatment and withhold antibiotics in a child with peritonism and systemic illness.
optionExplanations.D: Delayed appendectomy is not appropriate in the setting of suspected perforation/peritonitis.
optionExplanations.E: Inadequate for a sick child with likely surgical abdomen.

source.quizTitle: Practice Quiz: Emergency Medicine - Abdominal pain
source.questionTextHtml:
Your investigations of Lotta show a WCC of 18, with neutrophilia, an enlarged appendix measuring 8mm and a moderate amount of free abdominal fluid. Lotta remains febrile and lethargic and has now generalized guarding. Which one of the following is the most appropriate next step?

Intravenous antibiotics and plan for semi-urgent appendectomy after a few weeks
